meta.title: Automatic mutual recognition of occupational registrations (2021)
meta.summary: Worked example (P6). Automatic mutual recognition lets a worker registered in one state or territory work in another without a second registration (Mutual Recognition Act 1992, Part 3A, from 1 July 2021). It shows what the tool can and cannot cost: the second registrations' fees are outside the RBE and are a transfer, not a resource cost, and the scheme's mobility effect has no estimate in the evidence library, since the PC's licensing simulation leaves mutual recognition out. The Government's estimate of $2.4 billion over ten years could not be traced to its method.

source.description: Productivity Commission (2015), Mutual Recognition Schemes, Research Report

burden.title: Automatic mutual recognition: second registrations no longer needed
burden.description: The PC's aggregate annual cost of holding a licence in more than one jurisdiction, for the three occupation groups with an estimate (about 5% of licence holders in the eastern mainland states). The cost is the second licences' fees, so it is tagged as a government fee and left out of the RBE (RBM pp. 2, 4); the time to apply is not estimated by the source.
